newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo ends up, spot mixed.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo ends up, spot mixed.

text.p: Contracts on Shanghai's treasury bill repurchase market closed mostly up on Thursday, due mainly to the issue on the local bourse of 80 million A shares of the Shandong Lukang Co Ltd, traders said.
The annual rate for the most active seven-day contract rose sharply to 20.85 percent from 13.60 percent on Wednesday.
Total turnover rose sharply to 11.85 million from 3.63 million. One lot is 1,000 yuan face-value of treasury bills.
Traders said the issue of Shandong Lukang, the first big firm with a solid results record to list in Shanghai this year, attracted many institutional buyers.
"Early-maturing contracts rose early and became the day's leaders," one local trader said.
Traders said upcoming new issues and listings in both Shanghai and Shenzhen would support the early-maturing contracts at current levels over the next few days.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mixed. The combined volume of the eight-contract market rose slightly to 856,000 lots from 835,300 lots on Wednesday.
Traders said the returns on most contracts had begun to look attractive after falls early in the week, encouraging some institutional buying.
But most long-term investors stayed on the sidelines waiting for the listing of the new two-year note, the issue of which began this week, traders said.
The most active 10-year note, which matures in June 2006, fell to 114.68 yuan from 115.22 yuan on Wednesday. Turnover of the note was 0.51 billion yuan.
Traders said that after falling earlier this week, the annual return of the note has risen to above 9.5 percent, just a little lower than that of the new state debt issued this week.
